transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-26
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samira Patel (Redwood); Luis Martinez, Anya Chen, Marcus Doyle, Priya Nair, Tom Becker (Orpheus)

Summary:
Quick legal/ procurement checkpoint to confirm pricing commitment path, DPA redline expectations, and next steps to execute MSA+DPA. SE covered brief performance profile and options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Legal asked about egress, KMS, and audit logs. Ended with concrete action items and timing to get to signature sprint.

Topics: Pricing bands, commit levels, DPA redlines, KMS/Keying, audit logs, benchmarking window, SOC2/ISO references, escalation path for infra issues.

Action items (quick list): Jordan to send redline; Samira to share cost/latency doc; Anya to confirm legal asks.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we wanted to make this quick — check alignment on the DPA and pricing commitment so we can unblock procurement, does that timing still work for you Luis?
[00:12] Luis Martinez: Yeah this is good, we've got finance review next week so we need the redline and the committed numbers in time for them to sign off. I'm hoping we can get everything wrapped by mid May.
[00:21] Jordan Lee: Perfect, mid May is doable as long as we get the redline back and the commit level. Samira will go over the cost profile and the dedicated vs hosted delta in a sec.
[00:30] Samira Patel: Hi all — quick note, I'll keep this high level: for your expected chat agent plus embedding calls with 90th pct token bursts we see roughly a 25% cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated at the 100M token monthly band. If you add prefix KV caching and batching you'll see more improvement, but Dedicated helps with predictable latency.
[00:55] Marcus Doyle: Sorry can I interrupt — when you say Dedicated is predictable, are you referring to Redwood Dedicated or some VM-level thing? We need to be sure it integrates with our VPC and KMS.
[01:08] Samira Patel: Good question. Redwood Dedicated is our reserved GPU pool, it can be provisioned in a Private VPC mode for enterprise customers so you get customer-controlled networking and options for customer-managed KMS. There's an on-prem-ish flow we call Private Deployment if you need full air-gap, but normally Dedicated + VPC will do it.
[01:29] Tom Becker: On KMS — we need to confirm whether keys are customer-controlled in the private VPC option or if Redwood manages HSM. Also egress logging and audit retention periods are critical for our compliance team.
[01:43] Jordan Lee: Understood. Anya, do you want us to highlight specific clauses in the DPA for key management and egress audit retention?
[01:50] Anya Chen: Yes please. We need explicit language that keys are customer-managed for the Private deployment, and where Redwood manages keys we need key usage logs exported to our SIEM for at least 365 days. Also we have a data residency ask — some PII of EU customers must not leave EU regions.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll mark the Private deployment as a separate exhibit in the DPA and call out key custody options. We'll also include region pinning language for EU data.
[02:20] Luis Martinez: On pricing commitment: finance will accept a 12-month commit if we get a more favorable unit price and a clause to scale down after six months on 30 days notice. Is that something Redwood supports?
[02:33] Jordan Lee: We do support flexible commit structures. Typically the path is: 12-month commit with a step-down clause after the initial trial period. We can add a scaling clause — Samira, is that okay from a capacity/ops standpoint?
[02:44] Samira Patel: Yes. Operationally we can provision burst capacity and handle scale downs with a 30-day notice. For billing we usually have minimum monthly committed units and then usage above that billed at overage rates. We can build a stepped pricing schedule into the SOW.
[02:58] Marcus Doyle: I'd also want an SLA for tail latency. Our user experience team is sensitive to outliers — what does Redwood commit to for p99 response on your Hosted tier vs Dedicated?
[03:11] Samira Patel: For Hosted our p99 varies by model and sequence length, but we publish profile numbers. For Dedicated we can put an agreed p99 SLA in the contract — typically customers accept a per-model p99 target with credits on missed SLOs. We'll need to baseline with a short run to set realistic numbers.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: We'll include an SLA exhibit with measurable metrics tied to model/version. That exhibit will reference the benchmark run we'll do with your sample workload.
[03:37] Priya Nair: About the benchmark — we'll need to know what data is allowed and whether we can mask or synthetic-ize it. Also is the benchmark generating logs that might contain PII?
[03:48] Samira Patel: You can absolutely mask/sanitize; we also support redacted test payloads. Benchmark logs can be configured to avoid storing full prompts; we can do partial hashing and only collect telemetry needed for latency/cost.
[04:02] Anya Chen: On the DPA redlines I'm going to flag export controls and subprocessor lists — we need to know which cloud providers Redwood uses, and whether any subprocessors change during the contract.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: We can provide a current subprocessor list and commit to notifying you on material changes. For clarity, we use multiple cloud partners and a mix of on-prem partners for private deployments — we'll include that in the exhibit.
[04:24] Luis Martinez: There was a previous comment from Finance about vendor lock-in and migration assistance. Can Redwood commit to a data egress tooling path and reasonable export format if we need to move?
[04:36] Jordan Lee: Yes — we have standardized export tooling and we'll include a migration assistance clause in the SOW for refunds/credits if we fail to provide usable exports. We'll also document a runbook for data export.
[04:46] Tom Becker: On SOC2/ISO evidence — can you provide your latest SOC2 Type II report and explain any outstanding exceptions?
[04:53] Jordan Lee: We can share a SOC2 summary and an NDA-protected full report. There are no outstanding critical exceptions; we'll share the control summaries and the auditor contact under NDA.
[05:05] Luis Martinez: Great. Back to pricing detail: can you confirm the unit for embedding vs generation pricing? Finance was confused about tokens vs embedding unit counts.
[05:15] Samira Patel: Sure — generation is billed per token output/input. Embeddings are billed per embedding vector call (per chunk). We'll provide an example workbook to map your expected calls to estimated monthly cost.
[05:27] Marcus Doyle: Would you also include the uplift for private VPC/network egress fees? That was a hidden cost in some vendors.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: Yes. We'll surface egress charge assumptions and any cross-region fees in the cost workbook. If you want a flat fee for egress we can discuss a pass-through or capped arrangement.
[05:45] Anya Chen: For the DPA: the retention period for logs — we asked 365 days. Are you okay to put that in writing?
[05:53] Jordan Lee: We'll add a retention exhibit. For Hosted default is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private we can commit to 365 days for audit logs. We'll mark the difference in the DPA.
[06:05] Priya Nair: Slightly technical question — when you say KV cache and prefix caching, is that something we manage on our side or it's done in the runtime? If we do prefix cache at edge, it changes data residency considerations.
[06:18] Samira Patel: The caching is runtime-managed but you control cache keying; for Private deployments the cache can be deployed inside your VPC so data doesn't leave region. We can add that as an option in the exhibit.
[06:32] Luis Martinez: Okay — so next steps from Orpheus side: Anya will produce the legal redlines and data clause list by end of week; Finance needs the final price table by Wednesday; Priya will prep a masked dataset for the benchmark.
[06:45] Anya Chen: Yes, I'll send the redlines; I do have a couple of specific asks around liability caps and indemnity for model outputs — we need to tighten the language compared to your standard.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Understood. We typically have a mutual liability cap tied to fees and carve-outs for willful misconduct. We'll mark those areas in the redline and propose language.
[07:10] Marcus Doyle: Also, can we put a rollback plan into the SOW if a model update causes a quality regression? We need version pinning and automatic fallback to the last known-good model.
[07:20] Samira Patel: Absolutely — Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies. We can include a canary/rollback policy in the SOW and an automatic fallback route to the pinned model variant.
[07:32] Jordan Lee: I'll include a short technical appendix on rollouts, canarying, and fallback. That will satisfy the platform and the ops folks.
[07:40] Luis Martinez: Great. Anything else on compliance?
[07:44] Tom Becker: Just two things — encryption in transit/end at rest confirmation, and explicit network egress logging with SIEM integration.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: We'll add both: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and a SIEM export for audit logs with 365-day retention for Dedicated/Private.
[08:03] Jordan Lee: Okay let's recap real quick with next steps — Jordan to push redline DPA/MSA and summary by 4/29; Samira to share cost workbook and benchmarking runbook by 5/2; Anya to send legal redlines and specific indemnity/ liability asks by 4/30; Priya to prepare masked benchmark payload and agree on window for week of 5/5; Luis to confirm finance approvers and target sign date mid-May.
[08:30] Anya Chen: Sounds good. One question — what if there is a subprocesser change mid-contract? We need a minimum notice period.
[08:38] Jordan Lee: We'll propose a 30-day notice for material subprocessor changes and an opportunity to object during that window.
[08:46] Luis Martinez: Ok that should be acceptable.
[08:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a short Loom summarizing the redline high-level changes so review is faster.
[08:58] Marcus Doyle: Appreciate it, looking forward to the benchmark.
[09:02] Jordan Lee: Meeting adjourned, thanks all.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: "DPA redline draft (link)"; "Hosted vs Dedicated workbook (link)"; "SOC2 summary (link)"; benchmark runbook (link).
